column1: # PHP files retired without an ASP.NET port. One line per file: path<TAB>reason.
# scripts/php_reference_gap_inventory.py ignores lines with an empty reason.

column2: PHP CP CMS installer: registers content, content_access and control_items rows and lang strings for the PHP CP, builds PHP CP URLs and rebinds the PHP PDO link. ASP.NET serves Document Control from code routes (/cp/document-control-app via CpShopModuleRouteMap and CpNavTree), creates its schema with ErpDocumentControlRender.EnsureAsync, and opens tenant connections through ITenantDbConnectionFactory, so none of it applies.

Unreferenced predecessor of smsaero/send_sms.php: no operator row, CP page or caller posts to send_sms_old.php, and it targets SMS Aero's retired v1 gate (/send/ with an md5 password). The live smsaero handler (v2 /v2/sms/send with basic auth) is ported in CpSmsLegacyOperators and served at its PHP URL.

Unreferenced library: no PHP file includes it or calls any of its epc_rf_* functions, and nothing else reads the reg_fields columns it would add (field_category, available_for_approval, for_customer_approval, for_vendor_approval, compliance_tag). Its seed pack and approval checklist were never wired to a CP page, so there is no behaviour to port.

PHP deploy probe: require_onces config.php, dp_user.php and six price engine libraries one by one and echoes each step (with the document root, and the file and line of a failure) as JSON, to find which PHP include breaks ajax_auto_price.php. ASP.NET has no include chain (the price engine is compiled and wired through DI, so a missing piece fails the build or startup), and its liveness is /health. The probe also discloses server paths to anyone, so it is not ported.

PHP ops switch that answers 503 (X-EcomAE-Php-Serving: temporarily-deactivated) from the PHP front controllers while a flag file (.epc_php_serving_deactivated or /etc/ecomae-aspnet/php_serving_deactivated) exists, so ASP.NET can be deep-tested alone. Only index.php, epc_php_reference_router.php and the cloudpanel_*.sh scripts that touch the flag use it. Kestrel is the only server in the ASP.NET product, so there is no PHP serving left to pause, and the same operator intent (PHP reachable only under /php-reference/*) is enforced by PhpProductPathRedirectMiddleware.

Temporary PHP diagnostic for the /cp/control 524 hang: appends phase markers (elapsed ms since REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT, pid, URI) to sys_get_temp_dir()/epc_cp_trace.log when ?epc_trace or a flag file is set. Includers are the PHP CP shell only (cp/index.php, core/dp_core.php, cp/templates/bootstrap_admin/desktop.php, cp/modules/left_cp_menu/left_cp_menu.php) plus its reader epc-cp-trace.php. The PHP CP shell it traces does not exist in ASP.NET (CP pages are Blazor components with no include chain), and request timing there goes through the standard ILogger/Activity pipeline (Observability/EcomAeActivitySources.cs), so no phase tracer is needed.

PHP fallback that serves any readable file under /templates, /content, /modules, /lib, /icons plus favicon, manifest and sw.js straight from the docroot when nginx hands the request to index.php, with a small extension to MIME map. ASP.NET serves static assets only through explicit routes: PhpLegacyAssetBridge (/epc-static.php?f= with a prefix allow-list and path traversal check, /content/files/{**}, favicon.ico/svg, manifest.webmanifest, sw.js, /icons/pwa-icon-*.svg) and PhpAssetWrappers (*_css.php wrappers). The catch-all is deliberately not ported: it would also hand out PHP sources and config under /content, /modules and /lib. Its includers are index.php and epc-static.php (itself a PhpLegacyAssetBridge route).

PHP edge guard in index.php that 302-redirects /storefront/search-app, cart-app, checkout-app, orders-app, login, garage-app, profile-app and account-summary-app to the PHP storefront pages when nginx sends those thin ASP.NET stub URLs to PHP-FPM instead of Kestrel. Its only includer is index.php. In ASP.NET those /storefront/* URLs are real Razor pages (StorefrontSearchApp.razor, StorefrontCartApp.razor, StorefrontOrdersApp.razor, StorefrontGarageApp.razor and so on) answered by Kestrel itself, and redirecting them into PHP pages would invert the migration (PhpProductPathRedirectMiddleware sends PHP product URLs the other way), so there is nothing to port.

PHP CP CMS setup library: epc_oms_setup_pdo() opens a PDO link and epc_oms_register_guide_route() inserts or updates the `content` row (url shop/orders/oms-guide, content_type php, include /cp/content/shop/order_process/oms_daily_guide_page.php) and copies the parent's `content_access` groups so the PHP CP menu shows the OMS daily guide. Its only includers are the root one-off setup scripts epc-oms-menu-guide-setup.php and epc-cp-common-parity-setup.php. ASP.NET resolves CP routes from code (CpShopModuleRouteMap, CpNavTree) and opens tenant connections through ITenantDbConnectionFactory, so no `content` row has to be registered. The OMS guide page itself (oms_daily_guide_page.php) is a separate file.

PHP include that reads the next AUTO_INCREMENT id for shop_geo, shop_catalogue_categories, shop_tree_lists_items, content or groups by inserting and deleting an empty row inside a transaction, so the PHP tree editors (cp/content/content/content_tree.php, shop/geo/geo_tree.php, shop/catalogue/catalogue_editor.php, tree_list.php, tree_list_brunch_editor.php, users/user_groups.php) can hand out ids on the client before saving. ASP.NET has no client-side id preallocation: CpGeoTreeWriteService, CpGroupTreeWriteService and CpTreeListWriteService upsert the whole tree on save and the database assigns the ids, so the insert/delete probe has no caller.

PHP include that builds the `groups` hierarchy as DP_GroupRecord objects and a JSON dump (with $level/$parent/$count keys) for the webix group tree. Includers are PHP CP editors only: cp/content/users/user_groups.php, user.php, cp/content/content/content_tree.php, cp/content/shop/logistics/office_storages_link.php and cp/content/modules_control/edit_module.php. ASP.NET edits groups on /cp/groups-app (CpGroupsApp.razor) as a grid and saves them through CpGroupTreeWriteService, which orders and validates the hierarchy on the server, and the user page picks groups from the same table, so no webix tree dump is produced.

PHP data class DP_ContentRecord (extends DP_Content) holding one material row plus webix tree fields, with a constructor that sets defaults and the 'New material' caption (string 2220). Its includers are the PHP CP tree and form pages cp/content/content/content_tree.php, sitemap.php, cp/content/menu/menu_edit.php and cp/content/modules_control/edit_module.php. ASP.NET edits content through CpContentEditorService and its own record types and never builds a webix node, so the class has no consumer.

PHP include for the PHP CP left menu: maps shop/catalogue/products(/product) and shop/logistics/stock(/product) to link modes and prints the catalogue category tree as nested <ul class="nav nav-second-level"> via printCatalogueBranch(). The only includers are cp/modules/left_cp_menu/left_cp_menu.php and a PHP shell test. ASP.NET builds the CP left menu from code (CpNavTree / CpNavMenuService) and the catalogue and stock pages pick a category inside their own Blazor pages, so the PHP menu partial is not used.

PHP plugin that uses lib/MobileDetect to replace the template HTML with templates/<name>/phone.php or tablet.php for mobile visitors (cookie desktop_only / ?desktop_only and ?desktop_off switch back). No template in the repo ships a phone.php or tablet.php (find templates -name phone.php -o -name tablet.php is empty), so the plugin has nothing to swap, and the only other mention is a comment in cp/plugins/authentication/plugin.php. ASP.NET renders a single responsive chrome (PhpStorefrontDesktopChrome with its @media rules) for every device.

Unreferenced PHP debug script from the old supplier-API tester: it reads file and handler_folder from the query, checks that content/shop/docpart/suppliers_handlers/<folder>/<file> exists, then cURLs that handler with a fixed article (OC247 / KNECHT) and caller-supplied connection_options with TLS verification off. Nothing includes or links it (no PHP, JS or HTML reference anywhere in the repo). It is an open path-probe and SSRF-shaped helper with no caller, so it is not ported.

PHP CP script that prints window.EPC_APAI_DISCOVER, EPC_APAI_SOURCES, EPC_APAI_PRODUCT_LINES and EPC_APAI_IMPORTS (ajax URL, site key, active tab) for epc_auto_price_discover.js, behind an isAdmin check. No page loads it as a script src any more: content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php (epc_cp_apai_inline_discover_config_script) prints the same globals inline for the PHP CP shell. ASP.NET's Auto Price page is the Blazor component CpAutoPriceApp, which gets the ajax endpoint and site key from C#, so the bootstrap script has no consumer.

PHP CP footer script that prints window.EPC_SOCIAL_HUB (ajax URL, CSRF token, hub URL, site key and brand context) for the PHP Social Media Hub JavaScript. It is loaded only by PHP CP pages (cp/content/control/portal/epc_social_media_hub.php, cp/content/shop/tenant_hub/tenant_hub_main.php and content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php) and proxied by cp/content/control/portal/epc_social_media_hub_config.php. ASP.NET serves the hub ajax endpoint at its PHP URL (StorefrontPhpCpSocialAjax) but its CP pages are Blazor components that pass the endpoint, brand and CSRF in C#, so the window global is never read.

PHP CP footer script that prints window.EPC_VPE (ajax URL, site key, page key, layout blocks, block library, preview URL) for the PHP visual page editor JavaScript. Its only includer is the asset registry content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php for PHP CP pages. ASP.NET answers the editor's ajax URL (StorefrontPhpCpVisualPageEditorAjax) but has no PHP CP page that reads the window global; the layout and blocks reach the Blazor page through C#.

PHP CP footer script that prints window.EPC_PS (ajax URL, hidden menu groups and items, ERP module presets, industry defaults, style templates, storefront layouts, active theme) for the PHP portal settings page JavaScript. Its only includer is content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php for PHP CP pages. The ASP.NET portal pages are Blazor components that receive these settings from C# services, so the window.EPC_PS bootstrap is not read anywhere.

PHP CP footer script that prints window.EPC_OC (backend, order and customer ids, manager id, CSRF key, ajax URLs for delete, viewed, auth-with-user, pay/refund, comments, set status and print, and message strings) for the PHP order card JavaScript (order_card_cp.js). Its only includer is content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php. ASP.NET serves those ajax URLs at their PHP paths but CP orders are the Blazor component CpOrdersApp, which carries the order id and CSRF in C#, so the window global is not read.

Storefront-tree copy of the CP footer script that prints window.EPC_AGENT_CP (ajax URL ajax_epc_parts_agent_cp.php and CSRF key) for parts_agent_chats_cp.js; byte-identical to cp/content/shop/parts_agent/parts_agent_chats_config.php. Its only includer is content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php for the PHP CP page. ASP.NET serves the chats at /cp/parts-agent-chats-app (Blazor), which calls the agent through C# and never loads the PHP script, so the global has no reader.

CP-tree copy of the footer script that prints window.EPC_AGENT_CP (ajax URL ajax_epc_parts_agent_cp.php and CSRF key) for parts_agent_chats_cp.js; byte-identical to content/shop/parts_agent/parts_agent_chats_config.php. Loaded only by the PHP CP page through content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php. ASP.NET serves /cp/parts-agent-chats-app (Blazor, CpPhpParityTests maps /CP/shop/parts_agent_chats there) without the PHP script, so the global has no reader.

PHP CP footer script that prints window.EPC_SKU_MEDIA_CP (ajax endpoint ajax_epc_sku_media.php, CSRF key, root selector, language href) for the PHP SKU media manager JavaScript. Includers are cp/content/shop/catalogue/epc_sku_media_manager.php and content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php. ASP.NET serves the endpoint at its PHP URL (StorefrontPhpSkuMedia, StorefrontSkuMediaService) but the CP media page is a Blazor component that calls the service from C#, so the window global is never read.

PHP CP footer script that prints window.EPC_MULTIVENDOR_CP (ajax ingest URL, sample file URL, CSRF key, prices and storages URLs) for the PHP multi-vendor upload page JavaScript. Includers are cp/content/shop/prices_upload/multivendor_data_upload.php, content/general_pages/epc_cp_page_assets.php and the root deploy script epc-cp-common-parity-setup.php. ASP.NET serves the ingest endpoint at its PHP URL (StorefrontPhpCpMultivendorAjax) and the page as Blazor, so the PHP bootstrap script has no reader.

Dead mail probe: the first executable statement is exit, so the DocpartMailer test never runs. Nothing links or includes the file. ASP.NET sends mail through the ported notifiers (order, LPO, password, SMS/WhatsApp) and has no unused SMTP ping script to keep.

Four-line shim that only require_onces the finance schema content/shop/finance/epc_crm_schema.php. Its only extra caller is the one-off ops script epc-crm-cp-setup.php. The finance file is ERP (Devin) and stays a gap; this storefront-tree alias adds no tables or functions of its own.

Thin proxy that require()s the already-retired canonical content/general_pages/epc_social_media_hub_config.php. PHP CP pages loaded the canonical through epc_cp_page_assets.php; ASP.NET's social hub is the Blazor page /cp/social-hub-app (CpSocialHubService) and never reads the window.EPC_SOCIAL_HUB bootstrap.

PHP CMS data class DP_Template (id, name, html, phone/tablet flags, positions) used by the PHP front controllers index.php / cp/index.php / core/dp_core.php to describe a template row. ASP.NET has no PHP template object: storefront chrome is PhpStorefrontDesktopChrome and CP pages are Blazor components, so the class has no consumer.

PHP CMS data class DP_Module (caption, content_type, position, order) whose field names match the modules table. Includers are the same PHP front controllers. ASP.NET places modules from code (StorefrontModule, ControlPanelModule) and never builds a DP_Module instance.

PHP CMS data class DP_Content (url, tags, service_data, modules_array) used by index.php, cp/index.php and core/dp_core.php to hold the current material. ASP.NET resolves pages through routed endpoints and Blazor components (CpContentEditorService for the editor) and never constructs this class.

PHP webix tree node class DP_GeoNode for the PHP geo editors (cp/content/shop/geo/geo_tree.php, office_geo_nodes.php, content/shop/geo/get_geo_tree.php). ASP.NET edits geo on /cp/geo-app through CpGeoTreeWriteService, which upserts the whole tree and lets the database assign ids, so no webix node class is produced. Same reason as the retired dp_content_record.php.

PHP webix tree node class DP_GroupRecord for the PHP group editors (user_groups.php, user.php, content_tree.php, office_storages_link.php, edit_module.php) and get_group_records.php (already retired). ASP.NET edits groups on /cp/groups-app through CpGroupTreeWriteService as a grid, so the webix record has no consumer.

Deprecated alias that only require_onces epc_portal_automotive_spareparts_home.php when home_mode=auto_parts. The real home page stays a gap. The nero template is the only includer; ASP.NET home pages are routed Razor/Blazor surfaces and do not load this shim.

Unreferenced PHP data class DP_Product (catalogue product row plus images and offices arrays). No PHP file includes it or constructs it. ASP.NET product pages use their own records (StorefrontProductPage, StorefrontPhpCatalogueDemand) and never build this class.

PHP webix tree node class DP_TreeListItem for the PHP tree-list editors (cp/content/shop/catalogue/tree_list.php and get_tree_list_items.php). ASP.NET edits tree lists through CpTreeListWriteService, which upserts the whole tree and lets the database assign ids, so no webix node class is produced. Same reason as the retired DP_GeoNode and DP_GroupRecord.

ionCube-encrypted leftover under `cp/old php/`. The first executable line is the ionCube loader probe (`die` if the loader is present, otherwise print the get-loader.ioncube.com message and `exit(199)`); the rest is ciphertext. Nothing in the product includes or routes to this path. ASP.NET CP is compiled Blazor and cannot run ionCube bytecode, so there is nothing to port.

Dead cart plugin: the entire body after the file comment is itself commented out (`/* … */`), so PHP never merges cookie cart rows onto a signed-in user or clears `products_in_cart`. Nothing includes or routes to the file. ASP.NET cart merge lives in the ported cart/checkout services (`StorefrontCart`), so there is no live behaviour to port.
